# EP performance baseline

<!-- Generated by `make ep-perf` from `docs/probprog/ep-perf.json` (scripts/ep-perf.ts). Do not edit by hand. -->

Measured 2026-11-12 at commit `2493d806` on Apple M1 Pro (10 cores, 16 GB, darwin arm64 24.6.0), node v24.22.1. Medians of 9 timings for the micro rows and 3 runs for the items, after a warm-up, spread = (max - min) / median.

**Calibration** (a fixed pure-arithmetic workload, ms): 20.3 at the start, 20.0 at the end, mean 20.1 (drift 0.98x). **Load** (1-minute average): 3.5 before, 11.79 after. The calibration is also timed around every row, and `make ep-perf-check` compares each row at its own machine speed; absolute numbers here carry the load they were taken under (a niced process is moved between fast and slow cores as the load changes, so quiet runs are better).

## The shared grid integrator

One integral through the library entry point on a typical integrand per profile (`scripts/perf/grid-cases.ts`). "Integrand calls" counts every pass (the coarse passes that find the window and the fine one); the nodes are those of the final grid.

| profile | integrand | final nodes | integrand calls | time per integral | spread | ns per integrand call |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pair | Laplace likelihood, Gaussian location (kink at the outcome) x gamma scale (log coordinate) | 4320 | 6720 | 184.6 us | 61.5% | 27 |
| axes | bivariate normal, Gaussian mean x gamma precision x beta correlation (three axes, equal panels) | 13824 | 31744 | 2.11 ms | 11.1% | 66 |
| triple | Student-t, Gaussian location x gamma scale x gamma degrees of freedom (three axes, column form) | n/a | 35000 | 5.11 ms | 8.0% | 146 |
| line | softmax normaliser over eight classes along one Gaussian coordinate | 96 | 156 | 27.9 us | 7.2% | 179 |

The kernels under the integrators:

| kernel | what | size | time per call | spread | ns per node |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shiftedSum | shift, exponentiate and sum 4320 log weights (the size of a pair grid) | 4320 | 39.8 us | 17.5% | 9.2 |
| findWindow | window of a narrow peak at 3 from a start at 0 (801-node scans) | 801 | 129.8 us | 5.6% | 162.0 |
| tiltGrid | zoomed uniform grid of 64 nodes over a window of width 12, smooth integrand | 64 | 10.3 us | 9.8% | 161.5 |

## Operators: time per message call

The typical calls of each operator, recorded from EP runs of the atoms, models and programs and replayed under a timer (a fresh memo per call, as the engine gives). One row per operator, hook and call signature (`toN` the target port, then the argument families: `N` Gaussian, `Nv` vector Gaussian, `G` gamma, `B` beta, `Be` Bernoulli, `D` discrete, `Di` Dirichlet, `NG` normal-gamma, `W` Wishart, `NW` normal-Wishart, each with its dimension when above one, and `v` an observed value; then the shape of the parameters). `ep` is the message rule (or `tilted` for an operator that only has the tilted moments), `logEvidence` the evidence rule.

## Where the time goes: the share per operator

One instrumented run of each item (the registry's message, tilted and evidence rules timed from the harness: about 0.1 microseconds a call of overhead). Self time excludes the operators an operator calls (a plate calls its row); the gate is made fresh by each registry call and is not wrapped, so its own overhead is part of "engine and the rest" and its branches are timed as themselves.

Across the 26 items (74.50 s of wall time): 78.0% in operators, 22.0% in the engine and the rest (cavities, projections, scheduling, graph and tape bookkeeping).

## Hot spots seen

Written from the numbers above by the harness (the library is only measured, never changed here).

- Where the operator time goes: gaussian-gamma-precision 27.2% of the wall time, multiclass-site 12.8% of the wall time, negative-binomial-dispersion 8.8% of the wall time, gaussian-chain 7.8% of the wall time, likelihood-triple 7.4% of the wall time. The first of these integrate numerically on the shared grids (`tiltGrid`, `integrateLine`, the pair and triple grids), so the grid kernels are the lever on end-to-end time.
- `mvn-wishart` (the message to the precision matrix, Gaussian cavities) grows steeply with the dimension: d = 2: 529.9 us, d = 3: 6.80 ms, d = 4: 38.1 ms (the Bartlett quadrature has d (d + 1) / 2 axes).
- The slowest single message calls: mvn-wishart (to0 Nv4 v W4) 71.7 ms; mvn-wishart (to2 Nv4 v W4) 38.1 ms; mvn-sd-corr-group (to0 Nv2*4 GG B {groups}) 19.8 ms.
- Runs that spend most of their time outside the operators (graph and tape bookkeeping, the outer loop of a grid or hyperparameter search, projections): atom/gp-hyperparameters (2.2% in operators), program/changepoint-extended (18.6% in operators), program/kalman (12.4% in operators), program/cox (34.4% in operators).
- Each message call of a closed-form operator (`linear`, `plus`, `prior`, `gaussian`, `times-constant`) is a fraction of a microsecond, at or under the harness's own loop overhead, and the engine makes hundreds of thousands of them in a long run: the share of the engine around them is the rest of the wall time.
